sections.content:
95,865 people

were counted on the census as "mechanical engineers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Mechanical engineers direct the manufacture and manage the operation and maintenance of engines, machines, vehicle and ships' structures, building services and other mechanical items. They may also undertake research and design and development work.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "mechanical engineers" there were more men than women (93.2% compared with 6.8%).

This means "mechanical engineers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 93.2% and women made up 6.8% of "mechanical engineers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "mechanical engineers" included:

  • painters and decorators
  • refuse and salvage occupations
  • computer system and equipment installers and servicers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "mechanical engineers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "mechanical engineers", 13.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "mechanical engineers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "mechanical engineers" included:

  • rail and rolling stock builders and repairers
  • electrical engineers
  • building and civil engineering technicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "mechanical engineers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "mechanical engineers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "mechanical engineers", 6.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (92.3% compared with 7.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (88.9%) than self-employed (11.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Bristol, City of, this is in the region of the South West.
